topics.title: Trigonometric ratios of an acute angle

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the opposite side, adjacent side and hypotenuse for an acute angle and define sin, cos and tan as ratios of these sides.
Use cosec A = 1/sin A, sec A = 1/cos A, cot A = 1/tan A, tan A = sin A/cos A and cot A = cos A/sin A.

topics.title: Finding all trigonometric ratios from one given ratio

concepts.learning_objective: Explain, using similar triangles, that trigonometric ratios depend only on the angle, and that sin A and cos A never exceed 1.
Find the remaining trigonometric ratios of an acute angle from one known ratio using the Pythagoras theorem.
Recall the values of the trigonometric ratios of 30°, 45° and 60° and how they are derived from geometry.
Evaluate expressions and solve simple equations involving the trigonometric ratios of 30°, 45° and 60°.

topics.title: Ratios of 0 and 90 degrees and solving right triangles

concepts.learning_objective: State the trigonometric ratios of 0° and 90°, identify which are not defined, and describe how sin A and cos A change from 0° to 90°.
Find the unknown sides and angles of a right triangle when one side and one other part are known.
Use sin²A + cos²A = 1, 1 + tan²A = sec²A and 1 + cot²A = cosec²A together with the angles for which each holds.
Simplify trigonometric expressions and prove identities by writing them in terms of sin and cos or by using the basic identities.
